content:
Krail waits a moment longer, pen balanced between two fingers, then sets it down beside the unsigned order with a small, deliberate click.

"You need not decide this instant, my lord," he says. His voice stays level, the tone of a man reading a scheduled item aloud. "The order will remain here. The estate's accounts will not close today, and neither will this matter."

He squares the paper against the table edge, aligning it so the blank approval space faces Nera directly. "I would only note, for the record, that the loss extends beyond damaged cloth and a scorched portrait. A shipping folio of some value has vanished from rooms that were locked. Locked rooms, my lord, imply keys, and keys imply the maid who kept them. That is the connection the ledger must reflect if the folio is not recovered."

Elise's hands tighten around one another at her waist. She does not speak. Liora shifts her weight from foot to foot, her blistered palm curled against her skirt, and opens her mouth—then closes it again when her mother's shoulder shifts a half-inch toward her.

"Should you wish the prisoners held," Krail continues, "they will be held. Should you wish them released to their quarters pending judgment, that too is within your authority. I will draft whatever you determine." He smooths his cuffs, one and then the other, and retrieves his key ring from the table. "In the meantime, I will verify what the fire actually consumed against the wing inventory. If the folio is ash, the record will show ash. If it is not ash, the record will show that as well."

He bows, shallow and precise, collects his writing case, and moves to the door. His footsteps recede down the passage—unhurried, evenly spaced—past the place where Magerrett stands just out of sight of the doorway, and fade toward the stairwell.

The room settles into quiet. The smell of wet ash hangs over everything, and Ilyra's ruined portrait leans against the wall with its painted eyes half-consumed. Liora's gaze moves from the unsigned order to Nera's face and back again. Elise keeps her posture steady, one hand still resting near her daughter. Isolde stands where she has stood all along, yellow eyes tracking the door through which Krail left.

The pen lies where he set it down.
